channel.title: Google Developers Blog - AI
channel.description: Latest AI-related posts from Google Developers Blog

item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: a faster model for general purpose robotics
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings strong spatial and embodied reasoning capabilities to a fast, efficient model built specifically for robotics. To help developers put these capabilities to work, the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity transforms the platform into a comprehensive workbench supporting rapid hardware bring-up, MuJoCo simulation, and closed-loop control. Developers can leverage these tools to transition from an unboxed robot arm to a fully functional real-to-sim-to-real application in an afternoon using natural language prompts and day-one support in the google-genai SDKs.

item.title: Accelerating development for massive Git repositories
item.description: Meet Another Build File Service (ABFS), Google's open-source content-addressable filesystem and build cache that cuts Android checkouts to <8s and builds to ~2m.

item.title: Unlocking Stable On-Policy RL on TPU with Bitwise-Zero Train–Inference Mismatch
item.description: How we eliminated floating-point train–inference logprob drift for on-policy LLM reinforcement learning across 64 Cloud TPU v5p chips using a generalizable four-part JAX and Pallas recipe in Tunix.

item.title: TPU Model Design Considerations and Optimization Guide
item.description: The newly launched AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-codesign guide provides hardware-grounded design rules to help developers maximize performance on TPUs for LLMs and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) workloads. Key principles include aligning reduction and output dimensions to 256 for systolic arrays, adopting LatentMoE to compress routed token traffic, and mapping parallel axes directly onto physical links.

item.title: Securing Your Agents: A Hands-On Guide to Agent Anomaly Detection
item.description: This guide walks developers through setting up Agent Anomaly Detection on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform to monitor AI agent telemetry and catch behavioral risks. It demonstrates how to deploy a sample customer support agent, trigger out-of-scope security findings, and configure proactive alerts using Cloud Monitoring and Security Command Center.

item.title: Agents are sessions, not requests: size GKE node pools for AI agent sessions
item.description: AI agent sessions remain active and idle for most of the workday, making traditional one-Pod-per-session allocations inefficient for cluster resources. By using open-source tools like Agent Substrate and AX on GKE, developers can park idle sessions in object storage to release compute resources while maintaining session state. This approach optimizes resource utilization and reduces Kubernetes node costs by up to 40%.

item.title: How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write
item.description: Agent Anomaly Detection (AAD) provides asynchronous, low-latency monitoring for AI agents by analyzing OpenTelemetry traces and logs to flag goal hijacks and tool misuse. Tested across five public security benchmarks, AAD successfully caught 87% of harmful instructions carried out by agents without adding runtime latency. Developers can integrate AAD alongside semantic governance and strict tool limits as part of a defense-in-depth strategy to secure agentic applications.

item.title: Catch Go bugs that fuzzing misses with Gemini and a constraint solver
item.description: How pairing Go's surviving compiler bounds-check traps with Gemini 4 Argon and the Z3 constraint solver catches latent out-of-bounds panics in Go code and uncovers a slice-capacity blind spot in go test -fuzz.

item.title: A2UI 1.0: Build delightful, fast, reliable, agentic experiences
item.description: A2UI 1.0 is an open protocol for generative UI that enables AI agents to render interactive, native screens across web, mobile, and desktop applications. Developers can leverage open-source renderer SDKs—including React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose—alongside agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Dart. The release introduces bidirectional function calls, swappable inference formats, and secure data binding to help teams seamlessly integrate generative UI into their product stacks.

item.title: On-Device Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech in Google AI Edge Gallery
item.description: Google AI Edge Gallery now supports on-device, offline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities for building developer-friendly voice applications. Developers can leverage ML Kit for optimized Android performance, or use MediaPipe Tasks and LiteRT for cross-platform open-weight model integration. This local pipeline seamlessly pairs lightweight speech models with on-device small language models like Gemini Nano and Gemma 4 to enable real-time streaming transcription and low-latency synthesis.
